svg.title: Complete task lifecycle: from session setup to feedback
svg.desc: The caller creates a RobotSession, which starts sidecars and connects Env. The task entry prepares actions, skills, and state; fastagent generates a sequence and builds its executor. Each step checks state conflicts, dispatches tools and Rails, and executes through adapter API, Env, and Driver. Successful results update ExecutionMemory by contract; later steps read the updated state. Failures are handled by execution mode. The task returns, and the caller exits the session to clean up resources.
svg.text: Complete task lifecycle: from session setup to feedback
Follow the default fastagent path for ordinary actions; stepagent differences appear at the relevant stages.
A. Open a session: configuration → Session (Env / API / sidecar launchers)
Session starts configured sidecars, then calls Env.connect()
B. Prepare planning inputs and select execution mode
fastagent: actions / skills + scene / WorldState → plan_task → validate sequence
Then build Agent, tools, Rails, and executor [§5 Capability gating; §7 Two-tier planning]
stepagent: build Agent → agent.invoke() → model selects tools step by step
See §7, “Task execution sequence: two orchestration modes”, for the differences.
C. Each ordinary action: read state → check → execute → update memory
loop Repeat until the task completes or stops
fastagent only: on a state conflict, snapshot and replan within max_replans.
Keep the old plan if replanning fails or is empty; unknown state is not a conflict.
Successful results update state and locations in ExecutionMemory.
Read current state in the next iteration to check whether later actions need to change.
Per-step feedback and failure handling (when enabled):
Recovery uses action, payload, and failure type; Trace / Diagnosis collect evidence.
fastagent continues or stops; stepagent passes results to subsequent model calls.
See detail diagrams for vision actions and compound tracking steps.
D. Return results and exit the session
Trace finalization fallback (if enabled) → Env.disconnect() / Driver.close()
After Env disconnects, Session exits sidecar contexts; with session handles normal and exceptional exits.
Trace finalizes at task end, with a fallback on disconnect; recovery after execution failure is not guaranteed.
